answer.feedback: Search for an additional mechanism that can explain experiment-dependent substrate residuals, rather than choosing among these rate laws. In E2, the models generally under-predict x2 (notably C9 around t=1 h and C8 around t=6 h), so they predict too much substrate consumption there. In E3, the best near-fit models disagree in direction, but C29/C20 over-predict x2 around t=7 h and C40/C9 under-predict it around t=11 h; test whether the kinetics or another process changes across these operating conditions. E1 biomass is also generally over-predicted around t=9 h. Check especially whether the E2 and E3 residual patterns correspond to low- versus high-substrate operation; the supplied results do not identify their substrate levels.
answer.reasoning: No candidate meets the acceptance rule: every fit exceeds its 95% chi-square limit. C9 is close but still fails; C40 also has an imprecisely estimated Ki, and C20 has an imprecisely estimated m. C29 has precise parameters but still fails the fit limit, and not all starting points converged to it. Therefore none can be accepted. The residual patterns across experiments warrant another search rather than stopping as inconclusive.
